Issue body:
### Describe the bug

`kit.svelte.dev` is not complying to the [General Data Protection Regulation](https://gdpr-info.eu/) (GDPR), and if someone in Europe files a complaint, the Svelte team will have to deal with fines ["up to $11.03 million or two percent of the company's annual revenue, whichever is greater."](https://www.spirion.com/blog/gdpr-fines-increase/#:~:text=A%20lower%2Dlevel%20GDPR%20violation,annual%20revenue%2C%20whichever%20is%20greater.)

### Reproduction

1. Go to https://kit.svelte.dev
2. Scroll down to "deploy anywhere."
3. Depending on your location, you will see your exact location on the globe; that part of the website violates [GDPR Article 7](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679&from=FR#d1e2001-1-1) because the server uses geolocation data without the user's consent.
   https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/blob/3f7af7ac72e390ffa1f59d780a41e5cf71dff852/sites/kit.svelte.dev/src/routes/edge.svg/%2Bserver.js#L123-L126

Here is the result on my screen:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104603218/207915427-eef01f16-4ced-44a9-8d1c-c6f158caee43.png)


### Logs

```Shell
N/A
```


### System Info

```Shell
N/A
```


### Severity

annoyance

### Additional Information

*(the above dropdown was left as is due to it being inapplicable to this type of issue)*

I am sorry to be the bad cop here, especially after SvelteKit reaching v1. However, although I am not residing in Europe, it was necessary for me to report the issue, so the Svelte team, and possibly Vercel, could re-assess its best practices regarding user privacy. About a few months ago, I ran into an issue on Angular's issue tracker about [GDPR noncompliance](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/45541), and [I said the following](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/45541#issuecomment-1272337147) to try to stir up a faster response there after months of relative inactivity:

> What is the explanation for this? Why is the [angular] team not responding to something that involves potential litigation? Just because Angular is a Google project does not mean Google's analytics can be used without consent.

The same thing applies here. Just because the SvelteKit website runs on Vercel does not mean it can use Vercel's geolocation APIs without consent.

GDPR Article 7 Talks about `Conditions for consent` 

_(Take note of the word `processing`,  `data subject` and `personal data`)_

> 1.   Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data.
> 2.   If the data subject's consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. Any part of such a declaration which constitutes an infringement of this Regulation shall not be binding.
> 3.   The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time. The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal. Prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed thereof. It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.
> 4.   When assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account shall be taken of whether, inter alia, the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract.


Important Definitions

> ‘processing’ means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction;
> ‘personal data’ means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person (‘data subject’); an identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity of that natural person;
> ‘consent’ of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her;

Based on what I have read and understand, I could say that this issue does have it's reasons....

I use the following css hack through userContent.css, in case it helps anybody:

```
@-moz-document regexp("moz-extension://[0-9a-f\-]*/blank.html") {
    
    .highlight .highlight-buttons {
        bottom: unset !important;
        background-color: #fbfbfb;
        top: 5px;
        padding: 3px 4px !important;
        border-radius: 3px !important;
        border: 1px solid #dedede;
    }
    
    .highlight .highlight-buttons:not(:hover) {
        opacity: 0.4 !important;
    }
    
    .highlight-button-save,
    .preview-button-save {
        font-size: 0px !important;
    }
    .highlight-button-save::after,
    .preview-button-save::after {
        content: "Upload";
        font-size: 18px !important;
    }
    
}
```

It is better to replace the regex bit with the exact iframe source. You can find it by using (web) inspector on the screenshot overlay. So your final `@-moz-document` rule should look something like `@-moz-document url("moz-extension://6d1dcb20-4749-4f53-3318-2c8ac341dc38/blank.html")`

This css does two things: one, it uses css pseudo selector to rename the `Save` button as `Upload`, and two, it moves the screenshot buttons (close, copy, download, save) from their default position of bottom-outside to the top-inside. This lets you take screenshots of pages with sticky headers, by simply scrolling to the top, where the buttons are. Title at retrieval: Ability to help a participant unmute themselves
Status at retrieval: closed

Issue body:
As a moderator for family videoconferencing with 20+ participants who are mostly tech-illiterate, and who need to be muted when they're not talking because they make crazy noises or have bad microphones, I've found the biggest usability problem to be that they don't know how to unmute themselves. EVEN IF YOU TELL THEM, and say "You are muted, uncle! Move the mouse and click the unmute button at the bottom of the screen!" and they spend 5 minutes looking for it (I wish I was exaggerating).

I understand that a participant can't directly unmute another for privacy reasons (I presume), but what would help tremendously here is the ability to _help_ a participant unmute themselves, by having a "Ask participant to unmute" action in the context menu, which would then show a big fat OBVIOUS centered overlay prompt on the participant's screen that says:

> $other_participant_name_if_set is asking you to unmute so they can hear you. Would you like to unmute now? [Unmute] [Stay muted]

If the request comes from someone who has not set their nickname, then obviously the message would be slightly different:

> Another participant is asking you to unmute so they can hear you. Would you like to unmute now? [Unmute] [Stay muted]

And make those "Unmute" and "Stay muted" action buttons BIG, OBVIOUS COLORFUL BUTTONS, not dark-blue hyperlinks (which are tiny and hard to see due to the dark background behind them).

Choosing "Stay muted" would probably dismiss the prompt for a minimum of 20 seconds.

Issue discussion (chronological; participant names pseudonymized within the case):
Comment 1 (source ID 753520753) | Participant 2 | created 2021-01-02T19:43:46Z | updated 2021-01-02T19:43:46Z
Source: https://github.com/jitsi/jitsi-meet/issues/8323#issuecomment-753520753
Would it be better to have a feature (as in Zoom) where they can temporarily unmute by holding down the space bar? Basically a push-to-talk (PTT). Then when they are done, releasing the space bar is all that needs to be done.


Comment 2 (source ID 753524157) | Participant 1 | created 2021-01-02T20:14:30Z | updated 2021-01-02T20:17:01Z
Source: https://github.com/jitsi/jitsi-meet/issues/8323#issuecomment-753524157
Push to talk already is implemented in the web interface, but not easily discovered (issue #8322). It does not seem to be implemented in the mobile version (issue #8324).

But what I am requesting here is something else than push to talk, because not every user is going to be able (or want to) use that, so I still need the ability to mass mute and then help individuals unmute themselves. It is also helpful to have a "prompt the participant to unmute with an un-missable super-obvious request overlay" feature in general because, I swear, I've lost count of how many times I've spent five minutes trying to get my non-technical users to find the damned unmute button at the bottom and click it. They really need something un-mistakeable that I can put "right in their face".

Comment 3 (source ID 753643820) | Participant 3 | created 2021-01-03T16:42:15Z | updated 2021-01-03T16:42:37Z
Source: https://github.com/jitsi/jitsi-meet/issues/8323#issuecomment-753643820
Dear @nekohayo,
we all know that a Moderator is able to mute another participant. Maybe at the same UI location, a Moderator also should be able to unmute. But by the other hand, this is a privacy problem: Especially if your participant isn't able to unmute by self, he probably don't notice that he was pushed "on air"!

BTW: Such an tech-illiterate participant may be unable to unmute because don't know about the "common used" **icons**. To my experience it's better to tell him "Please press the [M] button on you key board!". The same yield for [V]ideo, of course ...



Comment 4 (source ID 753646164) | Participant 1 | created 2021-01-03T17:01:00Z | updated 2021-01-03T17:01:00Z
Source: https://github.com/jitsi/jitsi-meet/issues/8323#issuecomment-753646164
As I've stated in the problem description above, I am not asking for a force-unmute feature. I'm asking about the ability to send an obvious UI prompt to the participant, right in the center of the screen, that offers them to easily unmute with the message (and button) suggested above. That's a completely different approach which is not a danger to privacy, because they can always decline, it's a conscious action.

As a workaround, if you self-host you can force starting all participants muted and let them know about the space bar PTT feature.
I have had better success by having practice sessions in advance and sharing with the participants [a cheat-sheet of shortcuts I put together](https://community.jitsi.org/t/jitsi-meet-keybard-shortcuts-cheatsheets-in-english-and-spanish-possibly-others/21013).

Source: https://github.com/jitsi/jitsi-meet/issues/8323#issuecomment-791460814
Actually, there is a different use case where moderator-enforced muting AND unmuting could be beneficial to users.

At least in Italy, jitsi-meet is beeing widely used by schools to guarantee distance learning to children during lockdowns. This often turns messy when children unmute themselves at the wrong time, or fail to do so, or even mute/kick other kids.

It would be extremely useful to give moderators the chance to center all powers on themselves, including the power to force-unmute a participant. The privacy issue is easily solved by enforcing the presence of an overlay stating that "during this call, the moderator has the power to do so and so" when a participant joins the meeting, and by applying some visual indicator that the user has been unmuted.

addLoadEvent = function(func){if(typeof jQuery!="undefined")jQuery(document).ready(func);else if(typeof wpOnload!='function'){wpOnload=func;}else{var oldonload=wpOnload;wpOnload=function(){oldonload();func();}}};

With some extensive debug sessions we tracked down the problem and found a reason at least on my installation.
@deepak-srivastava found that any CiviCRM specific scripts were not loaded when using the registration page while not being logged in.
I am using the WP plugin "EU Cookie Law" which was configured to block any scripts (Auto Block option)  until the user agreed to use them. That caused the plugin to do what it was told to do... stripping the scripts.
Confirming the popup and reloading the page got it working... 

To avoid "normal users" run into that problem, I switched Auto Block off for the time being as I do not use any "spying" scripts anyway.

Thanks @deepak-srivastava for taking time!

Title at retrieval: Unable to access /userinfo endpoint when access token does not contain PII
Status at retrieval: closed

Issue body:
In this scenario, I dont want the access token to contain any PII (personally identifiable information). If required, I want the resource server to get PII using  /userinfo endpoint.
As suggested by @fhanik (see [discussion](http://cf-dev.70369.x6.nabble.com/cf-dev-Intended-UAA-specific-user-identity-fields-in-JWT-access-token-tt4408.html#a4730)), this has been done using UAA configuration option 

``` jwt:
  token:
    claims:
      exclude:
      - user_name
      - email
```

But, when passing the access token without PII to the /userinfo endpoint, I get a 500 Internal Server Error.
Stacktrace indicates a null pointer exception while getting principal

```
: Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException
2016-09-14T15:51:34.16+0200 [APP/0]      OUT [2016-09-14 13:51:34.159] cloudfoundry-identity-server - ???? [http-nio-8080-exec-4] .... ERROR --- HomeController:        at org.cloudfoundry.identity.uaa.account.UserInfoEndpoint.extractUaaPrincipal(UserInfoEndpoint.java:55)
2016-09-14T15:51:34.16+0200 [APP/0]      OUT [2016-09-14 13:51:34.159] cloudfoundry-identity-server - ???? [http-nio-8080-exec-4] .... ERROR --- HomeController:        at org.cloudfoundry.identity.uaa.account.UserInfoEndpoint.loginInfo(UserInfoEndpoint.java:50)
```

Looking at [UaaTokenServices](https://github.com/cloudfoundry/uaa/blob/5cbf9c1b65598892e6f72966a1288e11f72e793a/server/src/main/java/org/cloudfoundry/identity/uaa/oauth/UaaTokenServices.java#L1020-L1035)

``` java
[...]
        Authentication userAuthentication = null;
        // Is this a user token?
        if (claims.containsKey(EMAIL)) {
            UaaUser user = userDatabase.retrieveUserById((String)claims.get(USER_ID));
            UaaPrincipal principal = new UaaPrincipal(user);
            userAuthentication = new UaaAuthentication(principal, UaaAuthority.USER_AUTHORITIES, null);
        } else {
            authorizationRequest.setAuthorities(authorities);
        }

        OAuth2Authentication authentication = new UaaOauth2Authentication(accessToken,
                                                                          IdentityZoneHolder.get().getId(),
                                                                          authorizationRequest.createOAuth2Request(),
                                                                          userAuthentication);
        authentication.setAuthenticated(true);
        return authentication;
    }
[...]
```

it seems that if email (ie PII) is not in the access token, then no userAuthentication/principal is set, which whould explain the exception.

Is there a reason why userAuthentication is only set if email (ie PII) is in the token ?

Thanks

Linked pages and attachments are not fetched. Issue retrieved at: 2026-10-18T17:10:14.695307+00:00 Issue last updated at: 2017-04-13T16:53:39Z Title at retrieval: Sanitizing metadata in uploaded files on the client-side Status at retrieval: closed Retrieved issue comments: 9/9 Issue body: The status quo is that it is possible to perform deanonymization by examining the metadata of uploaded files (I tried the demo interface and saw no hints about it). A whistleblower may be unaware of possible embedded GPS coordinates in JPG files, or author names in Word documents, etc. Globaleaks would give _a false sense of anonymity_, while the journalists who receive the documents will be able to connect the dots and find the identity of the submitter. Even worse, the police could raid the offices of a newspaper and confiscate all the computers, to do forensic analysis. The authorities would find the source of the leak even if the journalists themselves had no intention to help them. There is a related issue here: #1323, but meta-data is potentially more dangerous. I think that in an ideal case we could: - tell people about the dangers of metadata _before_ they submit anything - use client-side libraries to remove metadata before the data gets to the server. This should be done, at least for the most common formats like PDF, JPG, Word, Excel, Powerpoint - perhaps even display a summary of what metadata was found and removed before the submission. - metadata could be removed on the server too (though it implies submitters have to trust the server admins - which is too much to ask, in my opinion) Issue discussion (chronological; participant names pseudonymized within the case): Comment 1 (source ID 293305791) | Participant 2 | created 2017-04-11T15:45:20Z | updated 2017-04-11T15:45:20Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293305791 @ralienpp there was an implicit choice made to not scrub, AV scan, or try to analyze submitted files as they are loaded in the platform. There are tools for scrubbing metadata that are well made and shipped by default with Tails. There are many good reasons for keeping the interaction of core software small with formats that are notorious for providing RCEs. Further Globaleaks has a data retention policy that by default removes submitted data within 15 days For setups that use PGP the content of the files is stored encrypted on the server. If PGP is not encrypted the Whistleblower is informed in the interface that their intended recipients are not encrypting files. That warning might not quiet address the meta data issue and could be changed to include language about the risk of Personally Identifiable Information/Metadata. This --> FAQS Comment 2 (source ID 293307941) | Participant 2 | created 2017-04-11T15:52:18Z | updated 2017-04-11T15:52:18Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293307941 Current language: ```html Warning One or more of the recipients of this submission has not configured a PGP key. This means that the submitted files will be stored in plaintext on the server. ``` @ralienpp any suggestions? Comment 3 (source ID 293557895) | Participant 1 | created 2017-04-12T12:14:12Z | updated 2017-04-12T12:16:22Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293557895 Thanks for the feedback, I wasn't aware that it is so by design. I do have a suggestion. I apply the "mother test", basically I ask myself "what would my mother think if she read that?". What is PGP? What is plaintext? So what if it is plaintext? Thus I would add something like this: ``` Warning One or more of the recipients of this submission has not configured a PGP key. This means that the submitted files will be stored in plaintext on the server. If anyone (e.g. law enforcement agents who confiscated the hardware) gets access to the server, they will be able to read your submitted files. Ensure that the files do not have clues (in metadata or in their contents) that could be used to reveal your identity. ``` I believe it should be made clear to the submitter that: - someone who gets access to the server will also be able to read the files (not just the journalists) - their anonymity is in jeopardy if the docs contain references to the source If you apply the mother test again, you see that the next questions would be "what is metadata?" and "how to check it?". Therefore, this page presents an opportunity to answer the questions right away by providing links to tools or to a brief explanation. The fact that the tools are available does not imply that people are aware of them and will use them. I have not tried Tails yet, but I will do so (as I am helping someone set up Globaleaks and will train them about the whole thing). If Tails doesn't somehow patch the "open file" dialog to pass everything through the data sanitizer - that's bad, in my opinion. At the same time, if you make people perform extra steps at the final moment, some of them may actually give up (like a bounce rate on a web-site). In any case, I will find the FAQ and see what the rationale behind the decision was, in order to see a clearer picture. I'd appreciate it if you could give me a link to it (I didn't find it, but I found #663). Comment 4 (source ID 293584550) | Participant 3 | created 2017-04-12T13:55:23Z | updated 2017-04-12T13:55:23Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293584550 Thank you @ralienpp for your important feedback. So looking forward for comments like yours. I've some additional clarification from my side; About metadata, the premises are: - the journalist is and will have always to be be a trusted party in the process; - removing the metadata that can deanonymize the whistleblower without removing the metadata that can proove the malpractice (e.g. the name of the perpetrator or of the victim) is not possible. - technically it is even quite difficult to be sure to remove the metadata for every file as the metadata do not have standard formats. what we decided is: - to not remove automatically the metadata - to eventually offer the recipient to save the documents in a "safe" metadata-free mode by providing a print feature of it and giving the recipeint the possibility to download two files 1) the clean one (to use during work) 2) the original to use in a legal procedure if and when necessary. about the texts and the mention about PGP you are right, the language is cryptic, here we fail also because are so so so old texts; recently we are taking care of this. The choices that lead to that text, in two sentences and not more are: try to write a concise sentence, that do not require too much translations and that so won't have that much errors in the translations process that is where the more are inserted. now probably i would go to keep them short but eventually i would replace "PGP" with "Encryption" saying: "One or more of the recipients of this submission don't have encryption enabled". FAQ: yes they do now exists still :( \cc @fpietrosanti Comment 5 (source ID 293641552) | Participant 2 | created 2017-04-12T16:55:06Z | updated 2017-04-12T16:56:58Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293641552 Here is another revision of the text, that tries to elaborate the consequence of someone evil gaining access to the box. ``` At least one of the recipients of this submission has chosen to not use encryption. This means that the submitted files will be plainly readable on the server. If someone malicious breaks into the server, they will be able to read your submitted files. Ensure that the files do not have clues in their metadata or content that could be used to reveal your identity. ``` RE: Building a whistle-blowing system, unfortunately GL is just a component that needs to be integrated into a larger solution for hostile environments. Insecurity through frustation is a real problem. Comment 6 (source ID 293643998) | Participant 4 | created 2017-04-12T17:03:24Z | updated 2017-04-12T17:03:24Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293643998 Please consider while writing the text that not all whistleblowers are anonymous, in fact for what anti-corruption NGOs say us, most declare who they are, so encryption is meant to protect the information against unauthorized access, not to avoid disclosure of whistleblower identity. Comment 7 (source ID 293730469) | Participant 1 | created 2017-04-12T22:57:18Z | updated 2017-04-12T22:57:18Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293730469 We come from different places and have different requirements. For example, this happened in my country: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldovan_bank_fraud_scandal Members of the parliament are _purchased in bulk_ to make them join another party and vote "correctly". Judges issue whatever decisions are desired by those who pay them. People who criticize the government are harassed, a vocal critic of those in power was found dead with a "self-inflicted" gunshot wound, etc. Those who are supposed to find and punish the guilty are guilty themselves, so obviously there is no progress in these cases, even though "our best men and women are working on it as we speak". It is expected that any potential whistleblower is *very* concerned about their own life, so (if they had proper infosec training) they would: - remain anonymous even to the journalists; because if law-enforcement exerts pressure on the journalists (e.g. with rubber-hose cryptanalysis) - there's nothing that they can learn, *in principle*. - remove all metadata and other clues that could possibly unmask them Without proper infosec training they might just think that making a new email address like "theunknownunknown1935@gmail.com" is sufficient to remain anonymous. Unfortunately I have to say that despite all of the above, there are countries that are worse off than Moldova; that's why I believe that at least some basic safe-guards should be in place, at least for the lower-hanging fruits (common, well-documented formats). Comment 8 (source ID 293804617) | Participant 3 | created 2017-04-13T06:46:55Z | updated 2017-04-13T06:54:56Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293804617 Thanks for the feedback. I totally understand and see your point. After reading well the ticket i found out that this is totally inline with past he research path we always discussed. Let me elaborate why and which is the state. Technically the receiver is and can only be a trusted party It is technically iimpossible to remove all the metadata. It is technically impossible to discern good from bad metadata. This lead us for the moment to simplify the assumptions, leave the metadata scrumbling in responsibility of the recipient avoiding to make false promises to the user. But the points you are making are totally legit and i support them. In particular, is normal path we follow to - work on adding more clarifications to the user on the topic - working on simplifying the technical gergon to make the topic more understandable to the user It's a research topic kept open to: -Offer the possibility to show the user recognised metadata even asking to the user what to remove - Offer to the admin the possibility to enforce max removal if the scenario requires that. Remains true and legit what told by Nick that aside that this is inline with the research to do, we will never be able to point out that the technique implemented won't guarantee anything and that the best practice will remain to highlight that better (not perfect) specialized tools exist. Comment 9 (source ID 293958998) | Participant 1 | created 2017-04-13T16:53:39Z | updated 2017-04-13T16:53:39Z Source: https://github.com/globaleaks/globaleaks-whistleblowing-software/issues/1942#issuecomment-293958998 Alright, I got permission to join the project on Transifex and after I fill out the remaining strings for Romanian and Russian, I will try to make another iteration and suggest changes for the texts that involve complex matters. In the meantime, as a source of inspiration, I would like to share a paper I've read recently. [Obstacles to the Adoption of Secure Communication Tools.pdf](https://github.com/globaleaks/GlobaLeaks/files/920297/Obstacles.to.the.Adoption.of.Secure.Communication.Tools.pdf) Here are some highlights ``` Ten participants confused encryption with authentication. “Multiple encryption” was described as using both a username and multiple passwords to log in to an account. “Double encryption” was equated to two-factor authentication (P12). ... P3, P7, P8, P11, P13, P22, and P43 have not heard of encryption, and did not provide any deﬁnition. P1 and P59 conﬂated encryption with data encoding. P1 explained encryption as sending messages in “computer language: 01010011110100” (i.e., binary), and said “these messages can only be understood by computer scientists, hackers, service providers and governments. Lay people cannot.” P59 explicitly described encryption as sending text in “binary language: 122121122”. Other participants explained encryption as: ... 2) Making conversations “invisible” (P14). 3) Slowing down the process of understanding the data, but the company can still read the messages. “Basically, encryption is (no encryption + adding some time to send the data packets)” (P23). ... 5) Using a special language (P27, P32, and P35). If some- one (like a computer scientist) knows the language, they can decrypt the message (P26). 6) Using proxies to access websites. P29 believes that using proxies (encryption) protects against the company and government agencies, however, proxies are not legal to use. All participants, but three, believe that encryption protects against the unsophisticated attackers “who do not know how to hack”. ``` ``` The key takeaway from mental models research is that non-experts do not understand abstract security properties. They can only understand why a property matters in the context of a speciﬁc threat model that matters to them. ``` Thus, the texts should necessarily address the "what's in it for me?" aspect. ``` 57 participants (excluding P2, P4 and P5) provided various incorrect explanations of digital signatures: (1) inserting a USB stick into the PC to sign a document using a unique code, (2) scanning a hand-written signature, and then adding the signature electronically to a document, or (3) signing a digital document using a stylus pen. P29 described a digital signature as “a speciﬁc font type in Microsoft Word used to type names”. ``` There are more gems in the paper itself, enjoy the read! :-)

Issue body:
Hi all, 
according to the EU law on the management of the GDPR privacy and cookies, technical cookies must have a maximum expiration of 6 months.

On Volto, we have some technical cookies with infinite or indefinite expiration, namely '**lang**', '**I18N_LANGUAGE**', '**redux_localstorage_simple_blocksClipboard**' cookies.

It is possible to change the expiration of these cookies to
6 months? 

What do you think? 

Are there any particular reasons why those cookies have an expiration date so far?

@giuliaghisini I agree. We should make this configurable if possible and maybe even set the default value to 6 months (though, we have to take into account that Europe is not the entire world :)).

When we created those cookies the GDPR rules weren't that clear if I recall correctly.

Comment 2 (source ID 1034162265) | Participant 3 | created 2022-02-09T20:26:48Z | updated 2022-02-09T20:26:48Z

It would be interesting to have at least an idea of the other regulations and what they say. Of course having it configurable would be awesome, but it wouldn't solve the possible issue of having a website targeted at users from several countries. I could see at least one of our clients migrate to Volto in the next 2 years. But this is just me trying to look at my crystal ball, so who knows.

I heard, but I'm not entirely sure about this, that Japan has its own cookie/privacy law, for example.
@terapyon sorry for bringing you into this without notice, but perhaps you might have some info about this? Or maybe a pointer to where we could find these info? :D

@giuliaghisini Do you have sources for this? 

> according to the EU law on the management of the GDPR privacy and cookies, technical cookies must have a maximum expiration of 6 months.

I haven heard about or learned of any generic 6 month rule for technical cookies and have been working on the technical and legal setup for an international company with many European and world wide sites, also in Italy. 

There are a number of lesser known 'extensions' of the gdpr in some EU countries or existing national pre gdpr legislation that hasn't been cleaned up yet after implementing the new privacy laws per country.  One I learned of recently is that in Belgium you're not allowed to collect anonymous statistics aldo without using any cookies: you always have to ask permission.

It's great to have the expiry dates configurable, but the 6 monthts is not a European guideline AFAIK (Italian maybe?) and if there is one I would really like to know about its source.

Issue retrieved at: 2026-10-18T17:10:37.846907+00:00 Issue last updated at: 2018-10-31T21:20:20Z Title at retrieval: Privacy Disclosure for the Provider API Status at retrieval: closed Retrieved issue comments: 1/1 Issue body: **Open Letter from the JUMP Team to the Los Angeles Department of Transportation** Thank you for the opportunity to discuss the the guidelines surrounding data sharing. We have appreciated engaging in a dialogue with you on these important and ever-developing topics. As you know, the Los Angeles Department of Transportation (LADOT) is requiring implementation of the Provider API of Mobility Data Specification (MDS) for the Dockless On-Demand Personal Mobility Conditional Use Permit (CUP). The MDS requires production of certain categories of location data that may unintentionally endanger rider privacy without specifying how that data will be secured, stored, and used by LADOT. Rider location data, including precise GPS, timestamp, and route information (collectively, “Trip Data”), may create significant re-identification risk when combined with other publicly available information unless it is properly obfuscated. With very little analysis needed, patterns emerge that can reveal a user’s home, work, and travel, putting their privacy at risk. California’s recently passed Consumer Privacy Act addressed this issue directly by adopting a definition of Personal Data that almost certainly includes Trip Data. Uber is prepared to implement the Provider API in compliance with the MDS. However, we are concerned that, to date, we do not yet have a formal policy from LADOT explaining how Trip Data will be secured, used, and stored. Given the speed at which the MDS is being implemented, it will be critical to resolve these issues in the short term to protect the privacy of our riders. While we are in full support of standardization across cities, there is a wide range of actions that all cities must pursue to fully protect this data from bad actors, including hiring staff and setting up adequate processes, policies, and safeguards. In the coming months, Uber is ready to work with the LADOT and others to examine the MDS in more detail and find opportunities to better protect trip-related data while promoting wide standardization and establish industry best practices for data collected by bikes and scooters. In the interim, we trust that as a responsible data steward, LADOT will abide by the following data protection principles.
1. Security of Trip Data must be maintained by LADOT

Any government authority requiring production of Trip Data through the Provider API should secure Trip Data in accordance with standards applicable to Personal Information. To do this, the recipient must implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that are no less rigorous than accepted industry practices related to the protection of Personal Information, and shall ensure that all such safeguards, including the manner in which Trip Data is collected, accessed, used, stored, processed, disposed of, and disclosed, comply with applicable data protection and privacy laws. In addition, we trust that LADOT will restrict access to Trip Data to specific individuals within the city’s internal teams who have been granted the appropriate authorization and access rights.
2. Uses of Trip Data should be limited and communicated to riders

In light of the potential for abuse, the receiving government authority should limit its use of Trip Data to clearly specified objectives that are in line with its mission and statutory authority. For example, LADOT has stated that it intends to use the data for permit enforcement, communication of events, parking restrictions, and city planning. These are all sensible uses of Trip Data. However, Trip Data data may be easily combined with other government data sets for uses the public may find less acceptable. By committing to a set of objectives or data use guidelines beforehand, the government authority can demonstrate that it intends to be a responsible steward of this information. To ensure transparency, Uber may notify riders that their Trip Data will be shared with LADOT.
3. Trip Data should be obfuscated when stored at rest

The receiving government authority should commit to obfuscate user Trip Data when stored at rest in its network. In practice, this is the act of masking or scrambling personally-identifiable or sensitive data in order to control how the data appears in the output of a database query. This simple but powerful step would significantly diminish the risk of user re-identification if Trip Data is ever publicly disclosed via a hacking or government records request. More importantly, precise Trip Data is not required for the vast majority of use cases cited by LADOT. City planning uses cases, for example, are actually better served with data that has been aggregated to uncover behavior patterns.
4. Additional data sharing must be restricted

Data privacy is in the cultural spotlight, and users are afraid they have lost control of their personal data. Yet, in the discussion on github regarding authentication, it has already been suggested that cities will be able to clone auth tokens to share with other agencies and vendors.

We would like to reaffirm that the receiving government authority will resist sharing any data shared by the Provider API to any other public or private bodies in the absence of a formal agreement. Without understanding the safety measures or commitments of these third parties, Uber cannot measure and mitigate the safety risks associated with sharing data outside of this agreement.

Last, we recognize that LADOT is required to comply with the California Public Records Act (CPRA). We request that LADOT propose a plan to ensure that the CPRA is not used to share unmasked Trip Data with the the general public.
In the coming weeks, Uber looks forward to working with LADOT and others on an industry standard for sharing bike and scooter data that will be acceptable to all parties. With participation from all, we are confident in our ability to develop a forward-thinking standard that meets the needs of cities while safeguarding the privacy of riders. Regards, JUMP Team Issue discussion (chronological; participant names pseudonymized within the case): Comment 1 (source ID 434851867) | Participant 2 | created 2018-10-31T21:20:20Z | updated 2018-10-31T21:20:20Z Source: https://github.com/openmobilityfoundation/mobility-data-specification/issues/137#issuecomment-434851867 LADOT has reviewed the comment and we have include our a link to the guidelines for handling the data in the README. ref #154

I am using [Conversations ](www.conversations.im)(1.11.5) and chatting with two different partners, both using current version of Monal, all via jabber.de.

- If I send an image to partner**2**, the image is just displayed **as a link** to the jabber.de server to click it in Monal.

I did some work drafting a privacy policy, but I realized that the SVN or Git credentials could be considered personal information.  I reviewed #307, and I think we can make the following assertions about how we use the credentials:
- Moonshine itself does not save the credentials
- The credentials will be passed to user-configured third-party applications.  These applications may save the credentials.
- The user is not required to enter credentials - they can save the credentials with the third-party application directly, or they can use an external source control application.

@rat-moonshine, please verify whether the code is consistent with these assertions.

Another case that I considered was the "This is great!" and "I'm having some problems" interfaces.   However, these interfaces do not request any personal information or account information from the user - instead the requests are forwarded to the Twitter, Facebook, or GitHub websites.  So, I don't think this needs any special attention in the privacy policy.

If anyone else thinks of other collected data that may need to be considered for the privacy policy,please let me know.

I have checked through SVN and Git process on using the credentials, I confirm Moonshine do not stores any credential data to its local storage or neither to any server. While in case of Git, Moonshine provides option to re-use entered credential for the same application session - the entered credential stores to the memory as long Moonshine session is running, but I think this is irrelevant to an extent too. 

The Git authentication window is suppose to come if user do not have any credential already stored to the system keychain. It seems like once any Git command _push_ command executes with a credential, it stores to the keychain, and next time you don't even need to provide any credential. I seen the behaviour in Windows, too.

The bottom-line is, by executing any SVN or Git command with given credential through Moonshine, the credential may store to the system keychain (by SVN/Git application) but Moonshine has no control over it.

To get rid of the Referer I also added this to anonymize-log:

```PHP
function anonymized_logging_redirect( $value, $keyword ) {
	global $ydb;
	$table = YOURLS_DB_TABLE_LOG;
	
	$now      = date( 'Y-m-d H:i:s' );
	$keyword  = yourls_escape( yourls_sanitize_string( $keyword ) );
	
	return $ydb->query( "INSERT INTO `$table` (click_time, shorturl, referrer, user_agent, ip_address, country_code) VALUES ('$now', '$keyword', '', '', '', '')" );
}

yourls_add_filter('shunt_log_redirect', 'anonymized_logging_redirect');
```

> the tracking protection of Firefox no longer causes that some working bookmarks will be reported as broken! That's why Bookmarks Organizer needs the permission to read and modify the privacy settings and to control the tracking protection setting of Firefox beginning with version 2.0.0. Source: https://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/issues/14184#issuecomment-395493855
When login the first time through HTTPS, a secure cookie is set... The problem is that if an user logout and then attempt to login again through HTTP, that will fails because there is already a secure cookie set that of course cannot be sent through HTTP. Same behavior occurs for a session timeout when an user need login again. Basically, if a secure cookie is set, user will have to login through HTTPS only.

There are some browsers allowing setting secure cookies via HTTP protocol but that is a wrong behavior which has been recently deprecated (For instance: FF 52).

There are not reliable solution here. Once the secure cookie is set and if an user want login through HTTP, it will have to remove the secure cookie first. The annoying thing is that you cannot unset a secure cookie for a specific domain via HTTP protocol... The only solution I see here is to set specific session name for both HTTP and HTTPS but this could lead to side effects I think.

Dear fellow php programmers,

May I share with you the solution I have found to this problem of ours. As I understand, there might be a multitude of reasons all of which are having the same misleading presentation – the infamous "_Failed to set session cookie. Maybe you are using HTTP instead of HTTPS_" error. So, I guess at least some of you could possibly have the same _problem root cause_ as I had, so the following solution may be of help. 
I work under Windows 10, use Firefox 65.0, PHP version 7.1.6,  Apache 2.4.26, MySQL 5.7.18, just to give you the context. 

After many experiments, I just happened to have PhpMyAdmin 'http' authentication work fine, under php development server, with url having 'http://' schema. Simply speaking,  I issued a command in the terminal (`d:\WebSites\phpmyadmin>php -S 127.0.0.1:80 `), changed in phpmyadmin configuration file ("config.inc.php") authentication type to 'http', issued in the browser address bar 'http://phpmyadmin/', got a login form and was able to authenticate into my MySQL account. 

But, when I was trying to do the same under Apache, this misleading error message about problem with setting cookies presented itself. So, I went to see the cookies that had been set under the development php server, and I found them under the Storage/Cookies tab of WebDeveloper Inspector. When I repeated this operation to see the cookies set under Apache server, I noticed the strangest thing: the *path* on the set cookies was not an expected "/" but a "/D:/". 

So, I dived into the phpmyadmin code to find the code setting the cookies, one thing led to the other, and I found in "libraries/config.default.php" file this configuration parameter – "PmaAbsoluteUri" – the first of the TON of them with the following description (excerpt): 
>  In most cases you can leave this variable empty, as the correct value
>  will be detected automatically. However, we recommend that you do
>  test to see that the auto-detection code works in your system. 

So, guess what, I set the parameter to `'http://phpmyadmin/'` along with other "usual configuration parameters: 
> $cfg['PmaAbsoluteUri'] = 'http://phpmyadmin/';
> $cfg['Servers'][$i]['auth_type'] = 'cookie';
> /* Server parameters */
> $cfg['Servers'][$i]['host'] = 'phpmyadmin';
> $cfg['Servers'][$i]['compress'] = false;
> $cfg['Servers'][$i]['AllowNoPassword'] = false;
 
Just to give more context, I had "phpmyadmin" domain name declared in my "C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts": 
> `127.0.0.2 phpmyadmin pma`

And in "D:\Apache24\conf\extra\httpd-vhosts.conf" file the most usual: 

> \<VirtualHost phpmyadmin:80\>
>     DocumentRoot "${DOCROOT}/phpmyadmin"
>     ServerName phpmyadmin
>     ServerAlias pma
>     ErrorLog "logs/pma-error.log"
>     CustomLog "logs/pma-access.log" common
> 
> 	\<Directory "${DOCROOT}/phpmyadmin"\>
>  		Options Indexes FollowSymLinks
>  		AllowOverride Indexes
>  		Require all granted
>  		FallbackResource /index.php
>  	\</Directory\>
> \</VirtualHost\>



That's it. The 'cookie' authentication works under Apache too. Hooray! But...
The 'http' authentication stopped working; this needs more debugging but currently doesn't bother me much. 

I hope, the PhpMyAdmin developers will notice this post and react appropriately.

Issue body:
`UploadMediaPresenter.java` uses Geocoder in the `reverseGeoCode` method.
This usage has several problems:
- Requires a geocoding backend such as Google Play Services, which is not always available and reliable ([example](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki//e/_(operating_system))).
- [Apparently](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16258898/does-android-geocoder-work-only-with-internet-connection) uses the network.
- Possibly a Wikimedia privacy violation, as Geocoder sends the user's picture location to a third-party service.

We already use a [small offline geocoding library](https://github.com/coordinates2country/coordinates2country-android), it could be used for this too. We only need the country, not full address.

Issue body:
Hello everyone,
In Matomo 3.13.6 or newer it should be possible to operate the Matomo analytics solution without cookies (https://matomo.org/faq/new-to-piwik/how-do-i-use-matomo-analytics-without-consent-or-cookie-banner/).
As you already mentioned in the FAQs (https://matomo.org/faq/general/faq_157/) there is an issue with cookies, created despite the use of _paq.push(['disableCookies']) in following use cases:
* when you exclude yourself from being tracked using the cookie method or using the iframe opt-out method, Matomo will create a cookie piwik_ignore set on the domain of your Matomo server (a temporary short-lived cookie called MATOMO_SESSID will also be created).
* when you’re asking for consent before tracking visitors, two cookies may be created: mtm_consent and mtm_consent_removed.
* _pk_testcookie is also created without any identifier and is directly deleted (it is only used to check whether the visitor’s browser supports cookies).

Using the standard iframe opt-out method on our site we can confirm, that wenn users change their opt-out in our Privacy-Page, where the Matomo opt-out is embedded, following cookies are being created:
* _pk_id.<websiteID>.<domainHash>
* _pk_ses.<websiteID>.<domainHash>
* mtm_consent or respectively mtm_consent_removed.

This issue means, that there is currently no GDPR-compliant way to operate Matomo without cookies, because the opt-out option is a "must" as visitors should be able to change their opt-in for analytics any/multiple times.  "_pk_id" and "_pk_sess"-Cookies require a cookie-banner as they are not essential for the website operation in terms of Art. 6.1(f) GDPR.  The use of "MATOMO_SESSID" for security reasons and  "mtm_consent/mtm_consent_removed"-cookies to save the opt-in/-out state of user's consent can be viewed as essential, if there is no way to avoid them technically.

We had unfortunately to remove Matomo from our site, because the cooke-less operation is the only option for us.

Is there a possiblity that this issue will be solved and wenn (especially the setting "_pk_id" and "_pk_sess"-Cookies)? 

The cookie-less operation of Matomo is important for public entities and all website owners, who do not make e-commerce or other business with the need for high accuracy of reports. Which means, that the issue is actually concerning **a very large group of users**.

Issue body:
## Summary

ubuntu.com/security/cve gives you the option to accept cookies or "Manage your tracker settings". When you click the button to manage tracker settings, there are 2 optional sliders and a button labeled "Save preferences". If you leave both the "Performance" and "Functionality" sliders in the off position and click "Save preferences", it seems that preferences are not saved. The next page you visit will again prompt you to accept cookies.

## Process
1) Visit ubuntu.com/security/cve
2) When prompted, click the "Manage your tracker settings" button.
3) Ensure both the Performance and Functionality sliders are in the off position (default).
4) Click the "Save preferences" button.
5) Click a link to any CVE.

## Current and expected result

**Current result:** Even though I saved my tracker settings with Performance and Functionality turned off, I am prompted to either accept all cookies or manage my tracker settings.

**Expected result:** If I leave Performance and Functionality settings disabled and click "Save preferences", I expect my preferences to be saved. I expect when I visit subsequent pages I'll not be incessantly prompted to allow the site to collect more information from me.

## Browser details
Firefox 82.0 (64-bit)

It is not a trivial difference; with a different CSP that means you allow any code dynamically generated by a domain controlled by the author of the script to end up running in your webpages. It would be perfect to steal credentials; while instead with the current CSP only the code in the `user.js` file is the one that runs.

If this option is introduced then we might end up with most of the scripts being created needing `unsafe-eval`, leading to a generally relaxed security measure. What would be the response when people start to get hacked this way?

Perhaps if you can think of a way to grant it to specific scripts, that would be better; but the observation above still applies: my offering an option to remove the sandbox we are encouraging lax security.

##### Please read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/ghostery/ghostery-extension/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide before submitting an issue.

### Description

Ghostery Version 8.5.0 is applying 'Add Blocker' to the loading of utag.js and utag.sync.js files.  This is a tag management api platform and not directly an 'advertiser' vendor.   Site will use these files as a dependencies that page code will directly call.  Blocking these files will cause undefined errors and break the site. As Tealium's TMS is not tracking users and is a pure TMS, it should not be blocked by default. Additionally, companies use Tealium's TMS to provide their GDPR AND CCPA consent management via this script.

### Expected Behavior

Tealium or the utag.js and utag.sync.js files are currently listed in Ghostery's 'Essential' category.  This tag should only be blocked if 'Essential' tags are blocked. 

### Actual Behavior

Ghostery is blocking the utag.js and utag.sync.js files only when the 'Add Blocker' feature is activated and 'Essential' Trackers are left unblocked.  

### Steps to Reproduce

1. [activate Ghostery's Add Blocker feature]
2. [Navigate to 3m.com]
3. [review network traffic for 'Essential' tag utag.js and utag.sync.js ]
4. review debugger console for 'undefined' errors that are caused by blocking the 'Essential' tag used as a dependency on this site.

### Versions

+ Browser: Chrome Version 81.0.4044.138 (Official Build) (64-bit)
+ OS: mac OS X 10.14.6
+ Node: 
+ NPM:

Issue body:
Okay, so I have wanted to make my dotfiles public for ages. The main reason I haven't is because I'm scared to accidentally leave anything in there that I shouldn't.

Over the last few months I've been extracting any **secret** data. Secret data I don't really want in version control at all, regardless of whether it's encrypted this includes [sec.conf](https://www.weechat.org/files/doc/stable/weechat_user.en.html#secured_data), X.509 certificates/keys, `~/.gnupg/private-keys-v1.d`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa` etc. I store these offline but at two different sites. Even encrypted I don't to share the ciphertext with anyone. Most people seem to just stop here.

However I want to go one step further. Have a **public version** of my dotfiles and a **private version**. The reason for this is because the **private version** might contain things such as domains that are linked to me, my IPv6 globally linked address, usernames that I posess etc. While these things won't grant authentication they may still be used to map me.

Therefore I am going to have a **private version** as well. This would have the unsantized copy. I don't particularly want to push this to github, gitlab etc.

I am thinking that symlinking to a dotfiles directly may still be the way to go. I think this [bare repo method](https://developer.atlassian.com/blog/2016/02/best-way-to-store-dotfiles-git-bare-repo/) might not really work for me.

The other thing I am hoping is that friends can make their own **private versions** from my public version. If they had a suggestion they thought I might like, they could check out a copy of the public version, branch that, and send a pull request back.

I've included a picture to demonstrate what I am trying to do.

My question is should I bother with any "dotfile" tools. I noticed [these tools](https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/Dotfiles#Tools) in the Arch wiki?

I had a look at `yadm` and it looks most promising. Particularly because of the [bootstrap](https://thelocehiliosan.github.io/yadm/docs/bootstrap) feature. That being said, it might be better if I use something like [ansible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansible_(software)) or [Salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_(software)) for bootstrapping and deploying to my stuff.

The "bare repo method" you mention above is precisely how **yadm** works under the hood.

I think what you are asking for is a way to manage files in place, but have the content published to the Git repo be sanitized in a custom way. I think that actually might be possible, if you don't mind doing some of the heavy lifting yourself.

I think it's possible to set a "filter" attribute in a `.gitattributes` file that refers to a custom "filter driver" of your own design. Checkout the documentation here for filter. https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes

You could write a driver that is informed by a configuration file that you keep private. Whenever content is added to or updated in the repo, if it has the filter driver enabled, your driver has the opportunity to sanitize the data that gets put in the repo. Likewise, when data is checked out of the repo and placed in your worktree, the driver has the opportunity to change the sanitized data back into the real data (informed by your configuration).

That's the most seamless way I could image to manage a sanitized set of dotfiles. Perhaps that's an idea you could run with. This is also an idea that I think would be completely compatible with **yadm**.

I would say Ansible/Salt might be a high cost of entry for any friends that want to try to use the data. If you go that route, I suggest making the end resulting public repo, something simple that doesn't involve much more than a repo and bootstrap script.

Source: https://github.com/yadm-dev/yadm/issues/143#issuecomment-462477711
For `.gitattributes` consider the following minimal example:

    # .git/config
    [filter "clandestine"]
      clean = sed --file=clean.sed
      smudge = sed --file=smudge.sed
      required

This creates a filter named *clandestine* which calls [`sed`](https://linux.die.net/man/1/sed) with the script `clean.sed` for removing secret data and `smudge.sed` to restore secret data.
`required` means that the files will not be added if the filter fails (i.e., returns a non-zero exit code) for some reason.

The respective scripts are very basic and the idea is just that you don't want to expose your secret ip address `1.2.3.4` to the public but want to replace it with `MY.SECRET.IP.ADDRESS`.

    # clean.sed
    s/\b1\.2\.3\.4\b/MY.SECRET.IP.ADDRESS/g

    # smudge.sed
    s/\bMY\.SECRET\.IP\.ADDRESS\b/1.2.3.4/g

Now set which files should be automatically cleaned:

    # .gitattributes
    *.conf filter=clandestine

Add two files with the same content:

    # test.conf / test.ini
    Host 1.2.3.4
    Host 8.8.8.8

After adding the two files to the git `git add test.conf test.ini` you can verify that the filter actually worked:

    $ git diff --cached
    diff --git a/test.conf b/test.conf
    new file mode 100644
    index 0000000..7709ff4
    --- /dev/null
    +++ b/test.conf
    @@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
    +Host MY.SECRET.IP.ADDRESS
    +Host 8.8.8.8
    diff --git a/test.ini b/test.ini
    new file mode 100644
    index 0000000..3104ddd
    --- /dev/null
    +++ b/test.ini
    @@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
    +Host 1.2.3.4
    +Host 8.8.8.8

As you can see in `test.conf` the filter automatically removed `1.2.3.4` with `MY.SECRET.IP.ADDRESS`.

```
    User virtualmachine
IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_vm
```

1. The filter perl script will look for the sensitive comment block using the regular expression

Issue body:
- [x] *Encryption at the level of Orbeon Forms* – Encryption and decryption will happen at the level of Orbeon Forms, so the values of the fields marked as "to be encrypted" will never be sent to the database (let alone stored by the database).
- [x] *Form data* – When the value of a field is encrypted, in the form data the containing element will have the attribute `encrypted="true"`.
- [x] *Form Builder UI* – The "Control Settings" dialog will have a checkbox allowing form authors to mark a field for encryption.
- [x] *Persistence proxy* – The Form Runner "front-end" will always see unencrypted data, and it is up to the persistence proxy to encrypt and decrypt data as needed.  When saving data, the persistence proxy will encrypt all fields marked as "to be encrypted" in the form definition before passing the form data to a specific implementation of the persistence API. Conversely, when reading data, it will decrypt all the fields that have the attribute `encrypted="true"`.
- [x] *Form Runner homepage in admin mode* – On this page, admins will be able to select a form definition and trigger data re-encryption for that form. Re-encryption will use the search API to get a list of all the form data, and for each form data, will read it, encrypt or decrypt fields according to the form definition, and if any change is needed, will write the form data back.
* *Limitations* – On summary pages, encrypted fields won't be included in the free text search, and field search for encrypted fields will only be able to do exact matches.
* *Out of scope* – The ability to change a key is out of scope for this request for enhancement.

1. From the Form Runner home page, admins ask for a given `app/form` to be re-encrypted (for now we won't support re-encrypting `app/*` or `*/*`).
2. Based on the `app/form`, the persistence proxy dispatches the request to the appropriate implementation of the persistence API. Out-of-the-box, for now, we'll implement this only in the relational implementation of the API.
3. The implementation queries the data table to find all the versions of the `app/form` for which we have data. It then iterates over the `app/form/version`.
4. For a given `app/form/version`, it retrieves the form definition, iterates over the corresponding data, and for each runs `FieldEncryption.encryptDataIfNecessary()`, and writes back the result.

Impacted versions: 13.0

Steps to reproduce:
1. Login to the latest runbot 13.0 with the administrator user 
2. Go to Settings > Users and change the notification type from "Handle by Emails" to "Handle in Odoo" for the user "Marc Demo". Give the user "Administrator" rights on the sales app for easier testing.
2. Create  a new quotation for `Deco Addict`, add some line on the quote and either e-mail the customer or add him as a follower on the quote.
3. Log an internal note to `Marc Demo` (with an @ to Marc so he gets a message).
4. Login with the user `Marc Demo` and open the messages from the top. You'll see a message from `Mitchel Admin` with the message:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6352350/74220543-2f50c900-4cb0-11ea-80cd-df2049ca677c.png)


Current behavior:
The reply that was done by `Marc Demo` didn't keep track of the message type. The reply has become a normal reply which is emailed to all followers.

As the ping was an internal message from somebody internal to somebody internal the reply from the chatter on this message should also become an internal note. Issue body:
Hi everybody,

I am working on a plugin that will provide the possibility to schedule messages about a new issue on Facebook. In order to get a Facebook application I have to add the relevant parts about cookies and Facebook to the privacy policy. I think that's no problem for me to do it by hand, but it would be challenging for journals when they would want to use the plugin themselves. Also I think there other plugins that would face the same issue.

I thought about the situation that it would be great when plugins could provide the necessary information for the privacy policy. The best knowledge about the collection and use of personal information have the authors of the plugins. When the plugin would provide this knowledge journal managers would be able to use plugins that need you to extend your privacy policy without worrying that they might miss an important part for their privacy policy.

I also have thought about other ways to achieve this. Like putting the information into the plugin documentation so that you can copy it into your privacy policy yourself. But I think in the case of plugin updates it might be forgotten to update the privacy policy after updating the plugin.

To solve this I would propose a change to `AboutSiteHandler.inc.php`. By adding a hook call right before the `$templateMgr->assign` plugins could add additional information to the privacy policy.

What do you think?

Issue discussion (chronological; participant names pseudonymized within the case):
Comment 1 (source ID 475055654) | Participant 2 | created 2019-03-20T22:35:38Z | updated 2019-03-20T22:35:38Z
Source: https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/issues/4304#issuecomment-475055654
I would worry that having the plugin automatically augment the privacy policy would take control out of the hands of the Journal Manager, i.e. they wouldn't be able to arrange or modify the content how they liked (without modifying the code). My preference would be to put this into the documentation along with some suggested wording.

Comment 2 (source ID 482631996) | Participant 1 | created 2019-04-12T16:08:48Z | updated 2019-04-12T16:08:48Z
Source: https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/issues/4304#issuecomment-482631996
I see your point. And I think you are right that you don't want take away power from the _Journal Managers_. The idea for suggested wording is a good start I think (and I will include suggested wording in the plugin).

But I also think that suggested wording will become a problem as soon as a plugin is updated and the _Privacy Statement_ no longer reflects what the plugin does in some way. In such a situation the _Journal Managers_ have to realize that the plugin has changed in a meaningful manner. And I'm not sure what would be the best way for a plugin developer to notify _Journal Managers_ about changes like that. Especially when you have a multi journal installation where every journal has its own _Privacy Statement_ but updates are done by the administrator.

What would you think about an optional approach? So you can decide as a _Journal Manager_ if you want plugins to be able to extend your privacy policy automatically. This will enable the _Journal Managers_ that want to have control about the wording not to use the text provided by the plugin. But on the other hand _Journal Managers_ that don't want / aren't able to formulate an adequate _Privacy Statement_ can go with the text provided by the plugin.

Comment 3 (source ID 482755700) | Participant 2 | created 2019-04-12T23:54:08Z | updated 2019-04-12T23:54:08Z
Source: https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/issues/4304#issuecomment-482755700

If the JM is happy with the default wording, they just link to it; if not, they modify the link or insert their own text directly. (We could drive ourselves mad writing tools for this kind of thing and still never accommodate the approach everyone wants.)

### Description.
The Black Friday animated banner that appears in the dashboard has the following link: `https://yoa.st/bf-sale-2019?php_version=7.2&platform=wordpress&platform_version=5.3&software=free&software_version=12.6.1&days_active=30plus&user_language=fr_FR` on my site.

From a "plugin guidelines" point of view, it may appears as a violation (§7 & §11): it's tracking via ads.

From a GDPR point of view, it may appears as a violation too: by following the link I have no way to express my non consent to the collection of these data. In addition, I have no information regarding how this data will be processed nor if these data will be associated with the referer field of the http request. For many users who don't view the full url before clicking, it could be seen as "disloyal collection".

### Solution.
Removes ads from the plugin.

I think it might be possible to feed events in to Google Analytics without collecting any personally identifiable information (and hence triggering the need for a privacy policy that covers installing Toil, among other obligations).

The [Measurement Protocol](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/protocol/v1/devguide) would be the way to go. It requires [an `Anonymous Client ID` or `User ID`](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/protocol/v1/parameters#user), which they seem to think can be a unique value stored either on the user's device or on our system while simultaneously remaining non-identifying. I'm not sure how they come to that conclusion; surely if I have your ID number and your device also has your ID number, I can identify you by checking what ID number you have stored on your device.

Anyway, we could either lump all the hits together under one fake user, or use completely ephemeral IDs and try to stop the user's system from logging its own ID.

Hi @shivekkhurana 
thanks for looking at this issue.

> What is the difference between wakuext_ and shhext_ calls?
The difference between `wakuext_` and `shhext_` is based on whether you have `waku` or `whisper` enabled.

For the purpose of this task you probably don't need to call `updateMailservers`, it is only used once you are connected to one and signal to `status-go` that we want to receive message confirmations (I can elaborate on it, but you don't need to be worried about this in this task) from those mailservers.

Essentially you need to make sure that `connect-to-mailserver` ( https://github.com/status-im/status-react/blob/32cb09c9c68497ce152216067d2e00309baef686/src/status_im/mailserver/core.cljs#L221 ) is never called (or better, is called but noops), if the user has not enabled mailservers.
Once you do that, it might show some "connecting..." dialog as the app expects to be connected to a mailserver, and that's something that should not be shown if the user has not enabled mailservers.


> Also, having seen the API, does anyone thinks that renaming to "Mailserver" to "History Nodes" will create confusion or is everyone okay with incremental renaming?
This is a hotly debated topic :) I don't have a strong opinion myself, I defer to UX on the call cc @hesterbruikman @errorists 

This also will require some changes on status-go, as the setting needs to be persisted, I can help you out with that (of course you are free to work on it if you wish), for now you can pick a variable name and just update the re-frame db (similarly to what we do with `syncing-on-mobile-network?` for example).

Hope this is helpful, and ask any question, we're happy to help (you can ping us on discord as well if you want to have a quick chat).
